messages:
leah: Seeing intermittent failures in the sampleapp during uvicorn startup. It happens when we import AsyncClient at module scope and schedule a background task in startup. Error is RuntimeError: no running event loop.

sam: can you paste a minimal repro or the stack?

leah: gist of the app: 
```py
# app.py
import asyncio
from httpx import AsyncClient
client = AsyncClient()  # created at import time

async def background():
    await client.get('http://localhost:8000/health')

def start_bg(app):
    app.add_event_handler('startup', lambda: asyncio.create_task(background()))
```

leah: stack trace shows RuntimeError from asyncio.get_running_loop when client does some internal setup on init. Happens ~30% of cold starts.

sam: sounds like creating AsyncClient at import time is racing with uvicorn's event loop starting. AsyncClient (or underlying anyio) sometimes queries loop policy during init. creating it later in startup should avoid it.

ashley: we saw this in onboarding workshops. TL;DR: don't create AsyncClient at module import if you use create_task on startup. Construct in lifespan/startup and close on shutdown.

ryan: curious — does the SDK do anything special in AsyncClient.__init__ that touches the loop? we try to be neutral but anyio/uvloop interplay can be surprising.

mike: can we add a note in sampleapps and quickstart? new users hit this frequently. Also maybe add a runtime warning when AsyncClient is constructed and no running loop is found.

leah: repro steps I used: docker-compose up -> hit endpoint -> saw intermittent exception in logs. attaching truncated log: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages/anyio/from_thread.py", line 45, in somecall
RuntimeError: no running event loop
During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:
  File "/app/app.py", line 12, in <module>
    client = AsyncClient()
RuntimeError: failed to init client: no running loop
```

sam: quick workaround while we patch docs: lazy-init pattern in module is simple: 
```py
client = None
async def get_client():
    global client
    if client is None:
        client = AsyncClient()
    return client
```
then call await get_client() inside startup/background.

ashley: opened internal ticket RED-CLI-789 to add a short FAQ section and update sampleapp. Also flagged as DX bug.

ci-bot: linked issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/789 (internal)

sam: technical note for SDK team: consider whether AsyncClient __init__ can avoid touching loop state synchronously, or emit a clear warning. Also add typing docs showing sync-safe usage patterns.

ryan: detecting this reliably is tough, but a RuntimeWarning when get_running_loop() raises could save a lot of pain for users. We can gate it behind an env var.

mike: can we patch the sampleapp in the onboarding repo with the lazy-init and a one-line comment? low lift and high impact.

leah: I'll open a PR with the sampleapp change + update to quickstart. I'll paste logs and exact repro in the issue. marking triaged :white_check_mark:
